title: Silverpine QBR - Health, Economics & Roadmap Handoff
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted for Q2 pilot
summary: Quarterly check-in to review Silverpine's usage patterns, cost drivers, reliability incidents, and align on a short pilot and roadmap handoff. Redwood AE + SE presented cost-optimization levers (batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization), agreed to run a 2-week performance benchmark, and to deliver security docs and a revised pilot SOW. Customer expressed need for predictable latency for user-facing features and SOC2 evidence for finance/legal. Action: run bench, share pricing scenarios, schedule pilot kickoff 2027-04-11.
next_steps: Redwood to run 2-week benchmark with Silverpine sample payloads (Maya) - target start 2027-04-04
Alex to send revised pilot SOW and pricing scenarios by 2027-03-31
Maya to share recommended quantization/profile matrix and expected token cost delta by 2027-03-31
Customer to provide representative 24hr traffic snapshot and 5 sample prompts by 2027-04-01
action_items: Maya Ortiz: configure and run perf bench against 'silverpine-sample-v2' payload set - due 2027-04-11
Alex Park: send pilot SOW + pricing + reserved capacity options (monthly commit vs burst) - due 2027-03-31
Tom Reynolds: share SOC2 cert and compliance contacts internally and confirm any extra regs - due 2027-04-01
Diego Marquez: export 24-hour traffic and KV cache hit rates, send to Redwood - due 2027-04-01
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-03-29
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Park (Redwood AE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Tom Reynolds (Silverpine CTO), Priya Singh (Silverpine Eng Manager), Diego Marquez (Silverpine SRE), Hannah Cole (Silverpine Product)

Auto-summary: QBR style health check focusing on usage, cost drivers, infra reliability and next steps to pilot Dedicated capacity vs hosted API with cost/latency experiments.

00:00 Alex Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you all squeezing this in. This is Alex from Redwood, we're gonna run through the last quarter for Silverpine and then hand off to Maya for the technical readout.
00:17 Tom Reynolds: Thanks Alex, we got Priya and Diego on the line, Hannah's here too. Quick note, finance will want an updated cost forecast after this.
00:28 Maya Ortiz: Cool, I'll start with the usage trends we saw. So Silverpine's peak 95th percentile latency is about 340ms on hosted for the recent month, with the majority of spend coming from the long-form summarization route you call 'doc-summarize'. Token mix is heavy on context tokens (avg seq len 900).
00:50 Priya Singh: Yeah that's right, the summarization feature is our big consumer. We're seeing a lot of cold-starts from users and the cache hit for KV is low, around 12 to 15 percent.
01:10 Alex Park: Quick clarification - when you say KV cache, that's server side prefix caching we enabled on the Redwood side, right?
01:16 Diego Marquez: I believe so. Our app doesn't persist session context on the client side, so we're hitting full sequences a lot.
01:30 Maya Ortiz: Ok, so low prefix/KV cache hit means more per-token compute, which explains spend. Two levers we recommend: improve client-side session stitching to raise cache hit and use aggressive prefix caching for identical prompts; second, evaluate mixed-precision quantization which can cut per-token inference cost by 20-40% depending on model and perf targets.
01:58 Tom Reynolds: That sounds promising. The caveat is we need to keep p95 latency under 400ms for user-facing flows. If quantization adds jitter we can't do it.
02:12 Maya Ortiz: Totally, and that's why the bench we'll run uses your exact prompt set. We'll measure latency variance and fallback cases. For production we usually recommend canary small-batch rollout, plus the option to pin critical low-latency routes to a non-quantized variant.
02:35 Hannah Cole: Curious about Dedicated vs Hosted here — finance prefers hosted due to simplicity but engineering wants predictable throughput. Thoughts?
02:45 Alex Park: Tradeoffs: Hosted API (our Redwood API) gives easiest ops, pay-as-you-go pricing; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools, capacity guarantees and lower unit costs at commit tiers. With Dedicated you can also configure tighter autoscale and isolate traffic for compliance. There's an upfront commit discussion.
03:05 Priya Singh: For our Q2 pilot we want to prove latency and cost. If Dedicated reduces token cost enough and meets latency SLO, we'll push for reserved capacity. But we need a clear break-even analysis.
03:20 Jordan Lee: From CS side we'll help model the break-even with your traffic. Alex will send reserve commit options.
03:30 Diego Marquez: Security question: we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and KMS integration for customer data keys. Also confirm audit log retention.
03:40 Maya Ortiz: Redwood Private and Dedicated support KMS integrations and HSM via our partner KMS flows. We can provide SOC2 artifact and the compliance pack; audit log retention is configurable — default 90 days in the hosted plan, extendable for enterprise. I'll attach the docs.
03:59 Tom Reynolds: Great, legal will want that. Also any FedRAMP conversations? We're not fed customer now but want to know the path.
04:10 Alex Park: We don't have FedRAMP cert yet; we do roadmap items for higher compliance tiers and can map controls. We'll flag that as a roadmap ask for the account.
04:22 Priya Singh: On reliability — we had two timeouts last month, each about 4 minutes, a burst due to a model rollout during a peak. Can you explain how rollout fallbacks work?
04:34 Maya Ortiz: Yes, we have smart routing and automatic fallback policies. If a model variant is failing we route to a compatible variant or a cheaper region. In your case it sounds like a deploy coincided with high concurrency and autoscaler delayed new workers. We can recommend pre-warming and a canary window to avoid that.
04:56 Tom Reynolds: Pre-warming what exactly? Instances? KV caches?
05:02 Maya Ortiz: Instances and KV cache warm-up strategies; also temporary burst capacity to absorb launch spikes. We'll include pre-warm playbook in the deliverables.
05:22 Alex Park: Alright, now handoff to Maya for bench details and timeline.
05:27 Maya Ortiz: For the bench: we need 5 representative prompts and a 24-hour traffic snapshot. We'll run two parallel experiments: hosted baseline and a Dedicated config (if you want we'll simulate reserved capacity numbers with our cost model). Bench will record p50/p95 latencies, token cost per request, and variance. We'll also try two quantization profiles (8-bit and mixed float16) and a caching strategy.
05:55 Priya Singh: That sounds exhaustive. How long will it take?
06:00 Maya Ortiz: Setup is quick, runs two weeks of synthetic load to match your burst patterns; we'll start on 2027-04-04 and aim to present results 2027-04-18. If you want a condensed bench we can do a 3-day smoke but less representative.
06:16 Tom Reynolds: Two weeks is fine, need confident numbers for finance.
06:22 Diego Marquez: On instrumentation — will you provide token-level cost breakdowns? We need that for chargeback.
06:28 Alex Park: Yes, our Console will provide token-level breakdowns and route-level cost analytics; we'll also export CSV.
06:36 Hannah Cole: Any immediate quick wins we can do while bench runs?
06:40 Maya Ortiz: Yes: 1) short-term: increase client-side session stitching to bump cache hit, 2) short-term: reduce max context where not needed (trim system prompts), 3) medium: enable prefix caching for repeated flows. Those are low lift.
06:58 Priya Singh: We'll take action on the client stitching. Diego will lead.
07:03 Diego Marquez: Yup, I'll own that.
07:07 Jordan Lee: Alex — can you confirm pricing scenarios: pure hosted, hybrid (hosted + reserved for critical routes), and Dedicated reserved?
07:15 Alex Park: Absolutely, I'll send three scenarios with break-even points and suggested commit levels (monthly and annual). Expect that by 2027-03-31.
07:23 Tom Reynolds: Good. Also, are there any competitor risks we should flag? We've had internal talks about building a small internal infra for privacy.
07:31 Alex Park: The build vs buy tradeoff: in-house can be cheaper at very large scale but costs a lot in ops and skills. Competitors like Replicate or Sagemaker offer endpoint options but typically less tuned for LLM-serving economics; Redwood's differentiation is the inference runtime and the observability for token-level cost.
07:51 Priya Singh: One more — SLA. For Dedicated what uptime SLA should we expect?
07:57 Maya Ortiz: Typical Dedicated SLA is 99.9% with priority support loops and on-call escalation; we can surface exact SLA clauses in the SOW.
08:08 Tom Reynolds: Ok let's talk timeline: we want a pilot decision by mid-May.
08:14 Alex Park: Sounds reasonable. Pilot kickoff 2027-04-11, two-week bench, then decision workshop week of 2027-04-19. If results align, pilot runs through May.
08:26 Hannah Cole: For the pilot, will you provision a staging Dedicated pool or just simulate pricing?
08:32 Maya Ortiz: We can do a staging Dedicated environment for the pilot (short-term reserved) to measure real-world effects. That requires a short commit — we'll layout options.
08:44 Tom Reynolds: Fine. Okay last things — who will be our day-to-day contacts?
08:49 Alex Park: CSM Jordan Lee will be primary for onboarding and billing; Maya handles the technical bench and SE work. I'll be your commercial contact.
08:58 Jordan Lee: I'll schedule weekly check-ins during the bench.
09:03 Priya Singh: Perfect. Anything else?
09:07 Diego Marquez: No, thanks.
09:10 Alex Park: Great, recap: Alex sends SOW + pricing by 3/31, Maya kicks off bench 4/4, Silverpine sends payloads and traffic by 4/1, pilot kickoff 4/11, decision workshop week of 4/19. Action items in the sheet. Thanks all.
09:34 Tom Reynolds: Thanks all, appreciate the clarity.
09:40 (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript: transcription is sometimes garbled — product names like 'Redwood Dedicate' or 'prefix cache' sometimes mis-typed, filler words present.
